description: Private web task manager for Sebastian (Sebo) and Alomi, with a deliberately public read-only AI endpoint so ChatGPT can review, analyze, prioritize, and plan around live task data. The browser app itself requires Google sign-in. Writes are not public.

when_to_use: When the user asks to check or review their tasks or task list.
When the user asks what is overdue, due today, upcoming, or due through a future date.
When the user wants to strategize, prioritize, simplify, optimize, prune, rebalance, or otherwise think through their entire Lyfe task system.
When the user asks for a catch-up plan based on current overdue tasks plus upcoming workload.
ai_usage.owner_selection: Use owner=Sebo for Sebastian/Sebo and owner=Alomi for Alomi. If the current user's identity is not clear from the conversation or saved context, ask which person before fetching. Never guess between Sebo and Alomi.
ai_usage.shared_tasks: Tasks owned by All are automatically included in either person's results.

fetch_strategy.general_task_request: For general requests such as 'check my tasks', 'review my task list', 'help me optimize my tasks', or 'what should I work on', fetch the full active task system using through=2099-12-31 so future tasks are included as well as overdue tasks.
fetch_strategy.overdue_or_today_only: For narrowly scoped requests about overdue tasks or what is due today, omit through so the endpoint defaults to today, then use each task's status field to distinguish overdue from due_today.
fetch_strategy.specific_future_horizon: If the user asks about a specific future date or window, use that inclusive YYYY-MM-DD date in through.
fetch_strategy.catch_up_planning: When making a catch-up plan, normally fetch the full active task system, not just overdue items, so upcoming obligations can be considered before scheduling overdue work.
fetch_strategy.repeating_task_semantics: A very overdue repeating task represents one currently outstanding recurrence, not a requirement to perform one completion for every missed interval.

ai_usage.planning_guidance: Use dueDate, status, daysOverdue, frequency, task type, and the broader upcoming workload to reason about urgency and sequencing. When optimizing the system itself, consider whether frequencies are sensible, whether tasks are too vague, whether one-off tasks should be recurring or vice versa, and whether workload is clustered unnecessarily.
ai_usage.cost_guidance: Make one read request per user question when possible. Do not poll or repeatedly refetch to verify the same answer. A full-system read and a due-only read use the same bounded Firestore collection queries, so prefer the scope that best answers the user's question rather than trying to minimize returned rows.

owner.description: Whose tasks to read. Shared All tasks are included automatically.

through.description: Return active tasks due on or before this inclusive date. For a full-system strategic review, use 2099-12-31 so future tasks are included.

public_read_api.privacy: This endpoint is intentionally public and read-only. It exposes only task-planning fields. It does not expose emails, Firebase document IDs, notification tokens, authentication data, or stats.

private_write_api.description: Add and modify operations require a private per-person API key. Delete is intentionally not exposed by the API.
